sn22.88:1.1: On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Rajagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrel Sanctuary.
sn22.88:1.2: Now on that occasion the Venerable Assaji was dwelling at Kassapaka’s Park, sick, afflicted, gravely ill.
sn22.88:1.3: As in preceding sutta, down to:
sn22.88:3.6: “Then if you have nothing for which to reproach yourself in regard to virtue, Assaji, why are you troubled by remorse and regret?”
sn22.88:3.7: “Formerly, venerable sir, when I was ill I kept on tranquillizing the bodily formations, but now I do not obtain concentration.
sn22.88:3.8: As I do not obtain concentration, it occurs to me:
sn22.88:3.10: “Those ascetics and brahmins, Assaji, who regard concentration as the essence and identify concentration with asceticism, failing to obtain concentration, might think,
sn22.88:4.7: He understands: ‘… there is no more for this state of being.’
sn22.88:4.8: “If he feels a pleasant feeling, he understands: ‘It is impermanent’; he understands: ‘It is not held to’; he understands: ‘It is not delighted in.’
sn22.88:4.9: If he feels a painful feeling, he understands: ‘It is impermanent’; he understands: ‘It is not held to’; he understands: ‘It is not delighted in.’
sn22.88:4.10: If he feels a neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, he understands: ‘It is impermanent’; he understands: ‘It is not held to’; he understands: ‘It is not delighted in.’
sn22.88:4.11: “If he feels a pleasant feeling, he feels it detached;
sn22.88:4.12: if he feels a painful feeling, he feels it detached;
sn22.88:4.13: if he feels a neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, he feels it detached.
sn22.88:4.14: “When he feels a feeling terminating with the body, he understands: ‘I feel a feeling terminating with the body.’ When he feels a feeling terminating with life, he understands: ‘I feel a feeling terminating with life.’
sn22.88:4.15: He understands: ‘With the breakup of the body, following the exhaustion of life, all that is felt, not being delighted in, will become cool right here.’
sn22.88:5.1: “Just as, Assaji, an oil lamp burns in dependence on the oil and the wick,
sn22.88:5.2: and with the exhaustion of the oil and the wick it is extinguished through lack of fuel,
sn22.88:5.3: so too, Assaji, when a bhikkhu feels a feeling terminating with the body … terminating with life …
sn22.88:5.4: He understands: ‘With the breakup of the body, following the exhaustion of life, all that is felt, not being delighted in, will become cool right here.’”
